benefits.value: 11.1 h saved on this house's walls (about CAD 513)
benefits.detail: SBCA: about 0.129 framing man-hours per sq ft; 1033 sq ft gives 133 h; 22% of that is cutting (range 15 to 30%), half captured by the cell; walls are 76% of the pieces.

benefits.value: 2.7% cut waste vs 10% typical order allowance
benefits.detail: Acucut 1D nester on this trade's 359 sticks: 188 boards, 771.75 m stock for 750.76 m of parts (bundle-window constrained runs add about 0.5 points). Conventional allowance 5 to 15% (BuildingScience). Difference about 200 bf, CAD 140 at CAD 700/MBF (estimate).

FMI puts rework at about 5% of construction spend and 48% of rework on poor communication or data. If labelled, sequenced, pre-checked parts prevent 15 to 30% of this trade's rework (estimate), callbacks fall by 0.75 to 1.50% of trade spend.

cell_does: Cuts all wall members from the framing model: bottom and top plates, studs, jacks, kings, cripples, headers, rough sills, blocking.
Burns the stud layout onto plates and the label + QR on every stick; marks electrical box heights and bores cable holes in studs (see Electrical).
Bundles each wall as a kit: plates on top, studs, then openings, in the order the crew nails them.
cell_cannot: Build engineered headers or LVL beams: they come pre-made; the cell cuts them to length if under 6.1 m.
Sheathing: OSB panels are cut by hand or a panel saw add-on.
app: Build: 44 steps with pieces highlighted in the 3D model; Bundles: drop zones and kg per bundle.
Scan any stick to see where it goes and what it touches.

summary: Every plate, stud, jack, king, cripple, header and block of the 10 walls cut to length and nested from real stock, plates laser-marked with stud layout, studs burned with box heights and pre-bored for cable, bundled by wall in assembly order.
highlight: 373 wall members from the real run, house-wide nest waste 3.31% against a 10% order allowance; plates carry the burned stud layout.
routing: Acucut routing: the cell's nester groups this trade's parts by section and stock length, cuts them in bundle order (last-installed at the bottom), laser-burns the label, QR and every mark listed, and drops each bundle in its zone so the crew picks in install order.
